citeAs: Mahmood, N., Ghorbani, N., Troje, N. F., Pons-Moll, G., & Black, M. J. (2019). AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278.
creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black (MPI for Intelligent Systems)
description: A retargeted version of the AMASS (Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes) dataset, adapted for robotics and humanoid applications. AMASS unifies 15 optical marker-based mocap datasets into a common SMPL parameterization, covering 346 subjects, 11,451 motions, and over 42 hours of recordings. The dataset is intended for use in robotics research including humanoid motion.
name: Retargeted AMASS for Robotics
rai:dataBiases: Previous attempts to merge datasets standardize to fixed body proportions, which fundamentally alters the data. AMASS avoids this by working directly with markers and recovering full 3D body surface, preserving body shape variation. The dataset is limited to optical marker-based mocap and does not include facial mocap or full body scans for all subjects.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset unifies 15 existing optical marker-based mocap datasets. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet; several others were obtained privately or recorded by the authors (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab and SSM). MoSh++ was used to map marker data into SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. Results were manually inspected and problems corrected or held out.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During mocap sessions, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. A variable pose prior weight coefficient q is introduced that increases the pose prior weight as a function of the number of missing markers, to handle cases where multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of optical marker-based motion capture recordings from 15 different datasets, with varying markersets ranging in size from 37 to 91 markers. Source datasets include CMU, BioMotion, KIT, MPI HDM05, TotalCapture, and others.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MoSh++ was used to convert mocap marker data into SMPL body model parameters (pose, shape, soft-tissue). Due to inherent problems with mocap such as swapped and mislabeled markers, results were manually inspected and either corrected or held out. Each frame includes SMPL 3D shape parameters (16 dimensions), DMPL soft tissue coefficients (8 dimensions), and full SMPL pose parameters (90 dimensions).
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by themselves and the community, and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables new applications requiring large amounts of human motion training data, including animation, computer vision, and robotics. It provides the largest unified mocap dataset to the research community, enabling deep learning models of human motion.
rai:dataUseCases: Animation, visualization, generating training data for deep learning, computer vision, human motion modeling, and robotics (humanoid motion retargeting).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++ (an extension of MoSh) — an optimization-based method using SMPL-H and DMPL body models to fit 3D body shape, pose, and soft-tissue parameters to sparse mocap marker data. Uses Powell's gradient-based dogleg minimization implemented in the Chumpy auto-differentiation package.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The dataset contains motion capture data converted to SMPL parameters; no per-item annotation count is described.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No human annotator demographics are described; data processing was done algorithmically with manual inspection by the authors.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No annotation quality analysis or inter-annotator agreement metrics are described; quality was assessed via scan-to-model distance metrics.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform (e.g., MTurk) is used; data processing was done algorithmically.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation protocol is described; the data was processed algorithmically using MoSh++.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific timeframe for data collection is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No explicit imputation protocol for missing values is described beyond the variable pose prior weight for missing markers.
null_reasons.rai:dataLimitations: No explicit limitations section is provided; the paper focuses on improvements over prior work rather than dataset limitations.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No discussion of personal or sensitive information in the dataset; subjects are identified only by body shape parameters.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The paper does not describe the robotics retargeting manipulation; the evidence quote only discusses dataset expansion, not retargeting to robot configurations.

evidence.name: We introduce AMASS, a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization.
evidence.description: The result is AMASS, the largest public dataset of human shape and pose, including 346 subjects, 11451 motions and 42 hours of recordings and is available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de.
evidence.url: We make AMASS available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de , and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.

evidence.isLiveDataset: With MoSh++ it is easy to add more data and we will continue to expand the dataset. We will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by us and the community.
evidence.rai:dataCollection: We amassed in total 15 mocap datasets, summarized in Table 1. Each dataset was recorded using a different number of markers placed at different locations on the body; even within a dataset, the number of markers varies. The publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet. We obtained several other datasets privately or recorded them ourselves (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab and SSM).
evidence.rai:dataCollectionType: The publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet. We obtained several other datasets privately or recorded them ourselves (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab and SSM). We used MoSh++ to map this large amount of marker data into our common SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The source datasets all contain varying markersets ranging in size from 37 to 91 markers; AMASS unifies these into a single format.
evidence.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: We used MoSh++ to map this large amount of marker data into our common SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. Due to inherent problems with mocap, such as swapped and mislabeled markers, we manually inspected the results and either corrected or held out problems.
evidence.rai:dataUseCases: The consistent representation of AMASS makes it readily useful for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning.
evidence.rai:dataBiases: Previous attempts to merge datasets [21, 29] adopt a common body representation in which the size variation among subjects is normalized. This enables methods that focus on modeling pose and motion in terms of joint locations. On the other hand, such an approach throws away information about how body shape and motion are correlated and can introduce artifacts in retargeting all data to a common skeleton.
evidence.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: During a mocap session, markers may get occluded by the body due to pose. If multiple markers of a particular body part are occluded simultaneously, the optimization may result in unreliable and implausible poses. To address this, we introduce a coefficient q= 1+ (x/|M|)^2.5, where x is the number of missing markers in a given frame, |M| are the number of total observed markers.
evidence.rai:machineAnnotationTools: We used MoSh++ to map this large amount of marker data into our common SMPL pose, shape, and soft-tissue parameters. Similar to MoSh we use Powells gradient based dogleg minimization [34] implemented in the Chumpy [26] auto-differentiation package.
evidence.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: With MoSh++ it is easy to add more data and we will continue to expand the dataset. We make AMASS available to the research community at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de , and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
evidence.rai:dataSocialImpact: In summary, we provide the largest unified mocap dataset (AMASS) to the community, enabling new applications that require large amounts of training data.
evidence.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: With MoSh++ it is easy to add more data and we will continue to expand the dataset. We will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by us and the community.
